context: General topology: compactness by finite open subcovers or closed-set finite intersection property; no Hausdorff assumption
editorial_screening_reason: The open-cover and closed-set finite-intersection formulations are equivalent by taking complements and applying De Morgan's laws. Neither requires Hausdorff separation. Some traditions reserve 'compact' for Hausdorff plus quasi-compact; such terminology must be recorded as a context-specific convention rather than silently imported into the general topological definition. Euclidean closed-and-bounded is an equivalence theorem special to R^n, not the defining general-topology requirement.

formulations.text: A topological space X is compact if every open cover of X contains a finite subfamily whose union is X.

formulations.text: Equivalently, X is compact if every family of closed subsets of X that has the finite intersection property has nonempty total intersection.

terminology_note: In this convention compact is equivalent to quasi-compact; in some sources compact additionally requires Hausdorff. The existing independent quasi-compact entry is retained for contextual searching.
